correctness.rationale: For every p=3 mod 4 and even r>=2, J²=-I over V=Fp^r with x²+1 irreducible, so all nonzero vectors decompose into four-element J-orbits. With one representative vi per orbit and check columns (Jvi|-vi), X/Z elementary syndromes are exactly {±vi,±Jvi}, all nonzero and distinct; the r-row check has full rank. Each orbit contributes the same alternating tensor vi(Jvi)^T-(Jvi)vi^T; summing over all vectors vanishes by finite-field coordinate second moments (r>=2), proving symplectic row commutativity. All nontrivial weight<=2 errors have nonzero syndrome, while a zero-syndrome weight-three witness combining Xi Zi with a different qudit exists; every nontrivial stabilizer occupies >=ceil((p-1)p^(r-1)/4)>2 physical sites except (p,r)=(3,2), so the witness is logical and d_diamond=3. Radius-one ball size 1+4n=p^r equals syndrome space. Independent finite modular computations corroborated p=3,r=4; p=7,r=2; p=11,r=2 and actual stabilizer supports. Joint-Lee radius one is not standard quantum Hamming radius one.
